Published online:
September 1, 2026

Geographic focus:
Global (primary focus: US, Japan, UK, France, Eurozone)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
A global bond selloff is accelerating, driven by sticky inflation, rising oil prices (exacerbated by the ongoing U.S.-Israeli war on Iran), and deepening concern over G7 fiscal sustainability. Fed Governor Barr, considered a centrist, has signaled a willingness to hike rates at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting if CPI/PPI data don't soften — pushing Fed Funds futures to price a 66% probability of a hike. Japan's fiscal situation is rattling bond markets, UK and French sovereign spreads remain under pressure. Manufacturing data globally was broadly resilient, with Eurozone PMI at a 4-year high, though US manufacturing cooled on price concerns.

Relevance: YES

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 — Distinctly hawkish. A centrist FOMC member (Barr) explicitly flagging a potential September hike, combined with three prior dissents and market pricing tilted 2:1 toward a hike, represents a meaningful hawkish shift from prior positioning. The bond rout and oil-driven inflation pressures reinforce the upside rate risk narrative.
